record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Which finite simple groups occur as automorphism groups of chiral d-polytopes, where a chiral d-polytope is an abstract rank-d polytope whose automorphism group has exactly two flag-orbits and adjacent flags lie in different orbits?

evidence.quote: Problem 1 Determine which finite simple groups are automorphism groups of chiral d-polytopes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank d (or d-polytope) is a partially ordered set P with a unique minimum element and a unique maximum element, in which every maximal chain (flag) has exactly d+2 elements, and which satisfies the usual diamond condition and strong flag-connectivity. Two flags are called adjacent if they differ in exactly one element. An automorphism of P is an order-preserving bijection P → P; the automorphism group Γ(P) acts on the set of flags.

The polytope P is called chiral if Γ(P) has exactly two orbits on the flags of P and any two adjacent flags lie in different orbits.

Problem. Determine precisely which finite non-abelian simple groups G arise as the automorphism group Γ(P) of some chiral d-polytope P, for some integer d ≥ 3.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is partially solved. For rank d = 3 (chiral polyhedra), Leemans and Liebeck showed that every finite non-abelian simple group is the automorphism group of a chiral polyhedron, with the exceptions of PSL_2(q), PSL_3(q), PSU_3(q), and A_7. Subsequent work has addressed specific families (e.g., PSL(3,q), almost simple groups with socle PSL(2,q), and chiral 5-polytopes from alternating groups A_n by Conder–Hubard–O'Reilly Regueiro). The general classification across all ranks d remains an active area, with several recent papers (2022–2025), so the overall problem is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.claim: Recent partial results addressing the exceptional families.

status_evidence.title: Chiral polytopes of order 2p^m
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to investigate chiral polytopes with specified automorphism groups.
status_evidence.claim: Active research, full classification not yet complete.
